title: IRMAA Bracket Calculator

data_vintage: 2026 CMS Parts A & B premiums and deductibles fact sheet

title: Medicare Plan Comparison

title: Medicare Out-of-Pocket Exposure Modeler
description: Given a coverage structure, IRMAA tier, and a year of Medicare utilization, walks the actual 2026 cost-sharing rules benefit period by benefit period and returns the medical and drug out-of-pocket cost, total exposure with premiums, and a routine/rough/worst-case scenario spread.
data_vintage: 2026 CMS Parts A & B and Part D standard benefit parameters

title: Total Cost of Homeownership
description: Given a purchase price, loan terms, recurring costs, growth assumptions, and a hold period, amortizes the mortgage month by month, grows each recurring cost year by year, and returns the gross and net cost of ownership over the hold, a break-even monthly rent, and a cost composition breakdown.

title: Home Affordability (28/36)
description: Given household income, other debt, cash available, and loan terms, runs the front-end and back-end debt-to-income ratios, takes the binding one, and solves by fixed 60-iteration bisection for the maximum purchase price it supports, including a rate-sensitivity stress test at plus one and plus two points.
data_vintage: 2026 (ratios are lender convention, not statute; interest rate is user-supplied)

title: Rental Property Deal Screener
description: Given acquisition, income, and operating expense inputs, computes NOI, cap rate, cap rate on total cost, DSCR, cash flow, cash on cash return, gross rent multiplier, and break-even occupancy, then screens the deal against five common investment thresholds.
data_vintage: 2026 (all rates user-supplied; screening thresholds are conventions, not statute)

title: Rental Depreciation & Tax Shield Modeler
description: Given a rental property's basis, an optional cost segregation split with bonus depreciation, and income/tax context, runs the 27.5-year mid-month residential schedule plus any 5-year and 15-year components, tests the resulting loss against the passive activity loss rules, and optionally prices the section 1250 recapture and capital gain tax at an assumed sale. Offers both a corrected 27.5-year schedule (verified to sum to basis) and a legacy variant matching the original source spec's formula for comparison.
data_vintage: 2026.07 (MACRS 27.5-year residential; bonus depreciation per OBBBA and IRS Notice 2026-11; Rev. Proc. 2025-32 brackets)

title: Business Valuation Estimator
description: Three method small business valuation blending an SDE multiple, an EBITDA multiple, and an asset based floor, with user-set weights and owner-dependence and customer-concentration discounts.

title: Owner Salary Normalization
description: Separates what a replacement manager would cost from an owner's total compensation package, producing comparable seller discretionary earnings and normalized EBITDA, plus a neutral reasonable-compensation pattern flag.
data_vintage: 2026 (SS wage base $184,500; market wage is user-supplied)

title: Business Sale Tax Impact Modeler
description: Models federal tax on a business sale across asset allocation, section 1245 and 1250 depreciation recapture, QSBS section 1202 treatment, NIIT, state tax, and an installment-sale timing overlay.
data_vintage: 2026 (LTCG brackets Rev. Proc. 2025-32; NIIT §1411; QSBS per OBBBA)

title: Marital Asset Division
description: Builds a marital balance sheet with repeatable asset rows and models an illustrative split under a community property or equitable distribution regime, tracking separate property apart and showing tax-deferred and taxable-gain assets at an after-tax equivalent.
data_vintage: 2026 (state property regimes; no dated dollar figures)

title: Spousal Support Illustrative Range
description: Runs the same inputs through several named, user-editable guideline conventions for spousal support and shows the spread between them, plus a duration range based on marriage length. Presented strictly as an illustrative range, never a forecast or a single estimate.

title: QDRO Pension Split Modeler
description: Models a defined benefit pension split using the coverture fraction, or a defined contribution account split using a segregated balance, including early commencement, survivor benefit cost, and a COLA-adjusted lifetime projection computed through an explicit loop.
data_vintage: 2026 (no dated dollar figures; ERISA and plan rules govern)

title: Net Estate Value and Probate Exposure
description: Sizes the probate pool and the non-probate pool of an estate separately, and puts an approximate range, never a point estimate, on what probate administration would cost.
data_vintage: 2026 (probate cost ranges are practice approximations, not statutory schedules)

title: Estate Tax Liability
description: Works out the taxable estate after deductions, applies the federal exemption including any deceased spousal unused amount, and adds a state-level estate or inheritance tax where one applies. The federal exemption is permanent; no sunset copy appears anywhere in this tool.
data_vintage: 2026 (exemption $15M single, $30M married, permanent; top rate 40 percent)

title: Annual Gift Exclusion Strategy

title: Long-Term Care Cost Estimator
description: Compares what care actually costs across four settings: paid help at home, adult day care, assisted living, and a nursing home, correctly crediting facility settings (but not home settings) for avoided household costs, with a crossover-hours calculation and an insurance offset.
data_vintage: 2026 (national median care costs, survey based, user-overridable)

title: Medicaid Spend-Down Modeler

data_vintage: 2026 (CSRA $32,532 minimum / $162,660 maximum; individual asset limit $2,000; ten-state scope)

title: AI Content Disclosure (AI Act Article 50)

title: Extra-Semester Funding Gap Planner
description: Models the four cliffs that hit fifth-year and extra-semester students at once: the Pell 600% Lifetime Eligibility Used cap, federal loan aggregate limits, a scholarship semester cutoff, and the SAP 150% maximum timeframe rule. Produces a semester-by-semester fundable/not-fundable breakdown and ranks the cheapest gap-fill order.
data_vintage: 2025–26 federal aggregate loan limits (dependent $31,000 / independent $57,500 undergraduate); Pell LEU 600% (statutory); SAP 150% maximum timeframe. User-override fields on every federal figure.

title: Workforce Cost-per-Outcome Ladder
description: Enter costs, enrollment, placements, and retention for up to three programs to produce the full DOL TEGL 6-13 cost ladder (Cost per Participant, Cost per Employed Exiter, Cost per Retained Employee, Cost per Individual with Earnings Increase) plus Cost per Employed Day, benchmark flags, and a side-by-side comparison for a funder-facing one-pager.
data_vintage: DOL ETA TEGL 6-13 cost ladder definitions (statutory framework, changes on TEGL revision cycles); Massachusetts workforce RFP $7,500-per-employment-outcome benchmark; ~$26/employed-day national CPED benchmark. All benchmark figures are user-overridable.

title: Counterfactual Haircut Adjuster
description: Enter a program's total cost, enrollment, and gross employed-at-exit count, then set a baseline counterfactual job-finding rate, substitution rate, and creaming discount to net out deadweight, displacement, and cohort selection bias. Produces a haircut-adjusted placement count and cost-per-outcome figure alongside the unadjusted gross numbers, with a one-click handoff into the Cost-per-Outcome Ladder (#170).
data_vintage: Method-only tool: standard workforce program net-impact evaluation logic (sequential deadweight, substitution, creaming discount). No fixed benchmark constants — every rate is user-entered and overridable.

title: Lurking-Variable Reversal Detector
description: Paste your own stratified 2x2 table (any number of strata, custom group/outcome/stratum labels) to get per-stratum odds ratios, the crude pooled odds ratio, the Mantel-Haenszel (1959) adjusted odds ratio, and an explicit reversal flag when the aggregate and stratified stories disagree. The Berkeley 1973 six-department admissions table ships built in as the worked example.
data_vintage: Built-in worked example is a static 1973 historical dataset (Bickel, Hammel & O'Connell 1975, Science 187:398-404), never refreshed. Primary use is a user-pasted table.

title: Parallel-Trends & Placebo Checker
description: A difference-in-differences companion that tests the parallel-trends assumption instead of asserting it. Enter 3 or more pre-treatment periods for a treatment group and a control group to get a pre-trend slope gap with a t-test, an event-study table of period-by-period treatment-minus-control differences relative to a baseline period, and an in-time placebo test that reruns the estimate at a fake treatment date inside the pre-period. A classic single pre/post 2x2 tab is included for completeness only.
data_vintage: No live or refreshable data. The built-in worked example is an illustrative synthetic panel, not a historical dataset.

title: Exempt-Salary True Hourly Rate
description: Compare two exempt-salary offers on true $/hr — unpaid overtime, commute time-value + cash cost, and PTO forfeiture bundled in, with the crossover weekly hours where the ranking flips.

title: Unused PTO Forfeiture Cost
description: Price what use-it-or-lose-it caps and no-payout exits actually erase from comp: forfeited days, cap-drag on future accrual, and unpaid balance at exit, ranked by cheapest fix.
data_vintage: Pure arithmetic on user-transcribed employer policy - no external data, no state-law database

title: Interview-Process Burden & Offer EV
description: Price the sunk and expected-remaining cost (hours, PTO, travel at true $/hr) of every interview pipeline against the offer's expected value, with a continue/withdraw verdict and a portfolio ranking across up to 3 pipelines.

title: Statistical Reasoning Lab
description: Five deterministic labs bundled in one file: regression-to-the-mean (pre/post + correlation), survivorship bias (Wald's WWII armor problem + user selection-rate math), hot-hand run-length (closed-form expected streak length vs observed), base-rate/Bayes (prosecutor's fallacy), and a seeded-LCG deterministic p-hacking spec-curve multiverse (same seed always reproduces the same 16-path result).
data_vintage: Pure arithmetic + static historical reference (Wald WWII armor problem) — no live data, no vintage

title: Response-Rate Sensitivity Lab
description: Interactive nonresponse-bias teaching demo: enter an observed survey mean among respondents plus worst-case scale bounds for non-respondents, drag a response-rate slider, and watch the Manski-style worst-case identified interval sweep in real time. A second calculator finds the minimum response rate needed for the worst-case bound to clear a chosen threshold ('sign the effect'). Classroom-framed, not an analyst bounds estimator.
data_vintage: Pure closed-form interval arithmetic - no live data, no vintage

title: Levels-of-Analysis Lab (Ecological Fallacy)
description: Paste a group-level table (group label, n, mean X, mean Y) and get the n-weighted ecological (group-level) correlation, computed closed-form across group means. Compare it against a known or assumed individual-level correlation you supply, and the tool flags a levels-of-analysis reversal or magnitude-inflation risk when the two disagree. Ships with Robinson's 1950 published state-vs-individual reversal (textbook figures, informational) and a synthetic school-level income-vs-test-score example.
data_vintage: Robinson example reproduces published 1950 textbook correlation figures (static, informational only). School-income example is a synthetic illustrative dataset, not real data. Primary use is a user-pasted group table; no live data.

title: Credit-by-Exam ROI (AP / IB / CLEP)
description: Price which AP, IB, and CLEP exams pay off at a specific college: per exam, the fee plus study hours valued at the user's hourly rate, against the credit grant the user transcribes from the college's policy, valued at the user's tuition rate per credit and weighted by the chance the credit applies to the degree. Exams rank by net dollars with KEEP/DROP calls, per-exam breakeven credits, and keep-vs-drop totals. No policy database is stored; every policy figure is user-transcribed.
data_vintage: Exam fees are editable defaults (typical 2025-26 published per-exam registration fees, not a maintained database). Credit grants, tuition per credit, and approval odds are transcribed by the user from their college's own policy pages; no live data.

title: Growing-Family Marginal Cost (2nd+ Child)
description: Stack the true marginal cost of a second or later child against the current one-child baseline: USDA-stamped scale factors for housing, transport, food, healthcare, and other spend, childcare that stacks near full price after any sibling discount, flat FSA and child-tax-credit caps that do not scale, and the compound growth lost while savings are paused. Outputs gross and net monthly marginal, an 18-year total including lost compound, and levers ranked by monthly relief. No rate database stored; family figures are user-supplied.
data_vintage: Marginal scale-factor defaults are the USDA Expenditures on Children by Families report (2015-16 CEX, final edition) two-child ratios; FSA household cap $5,000 and child tax credit $2,200 are 2025-26 figures. All defaults are editable and every family figure is user-supplied; no live data.

title: Divorce House: Keep vs. Sell
description: Price the largest check in a divorce two ways: keeping the marital home (refinance the balance plus the equity buyout at one income, carry taxes, insurance, and an upkeep reserve) versus selling (net proceeds after friction costs, invested at your return, with a rent reset that inflates). Compares net position at 5 and 10 years, reports the housing ratio with an affordability verdict, and flags refinance qualification and the 80 percent LTV line. Every figure is user-entered; deterministic arithmetic, not legal or tax advice.
data_vintage: Every figure is user-entered (balances, rates, rents, appreciation, returns). No market feeds, no rate tables, no stored data. Outputs are deterministic arithmetic over those inputs and are not legal or tax advice.

title: Automation Payback
description: Rank automation candidates by payback before you build: monthly reclaimable value (hours saved per week times the loaded hourly rate, plus the error cost the automation eliminates) against total cost of ownership (one-time build amortized over the horizon, subscription, and a maintenance haircut on recurring cost, default 20 percent). Outputs a ranked table with break-even months and BUILD/SKIP calls, portfolio totals for hours reclaimed and net dollars, and a verdict naming the best candidate and the fastest break-even. No tool-price database; every figure is a user estimate.
data_vintage: No tool-price database: hours, loaded rates, build costs, subscriptions, and error costs are user estimates per candidate. The only fixed assumption is the maintenance haircut (default 20 percent, editable).

title: Scope-Creep Pricer (Change Orders)
description: Turn scope creep into a priced change order: compare a fixed fee against the hours actually worked to get the baseline rate, the effective rate, and the effective-rate decay percentage. Prices the unpriced creep hours at your baseline rate, produces the change-order price at standard and rush multipliers (1.0x, 1.25x, 1.5x), and checks the effective rate against a walk-away floor with a renegotiate-or-decline verdict. Pure arithmetic on user-entered project figures; nothing stored.
data_vintage: Pure arithmetic on user-entered project figures (fee, quoted scope hours, actual hours, floor rate, rush multiplier). No market feeds, no rate tables, no stored data.
